cdp.name: CDP
cdp.gloss: Customer Data Platform — the unified store of who your customers are.

perso.name: Personalization (1:1)
perso.gloss: Tailoring the message to the individual, not the segment.

genai.name: Generative AI
genai.gloss: Models that produce content — copy, images, replies — from a prompt.

agentic.name: Agentic AI
agentic.gloss: Systems that don't just generate, they decide and act toward a goal.

decis.name: Agentic decisioning
decis.gloss: An agent choosing what to say, when, how often and on which channel — per person.

bandit.name: Bandits / RL
bandit.gloss: The maths that lets a system learn which choice wins by trying and measuring.

cep.name: CEP
cep.gloss: Customer Engagement Platform — where this messaging actually runs.

geo.name: GEO
geo.gloss: Generative Engine Optimization — being visible inside AI answers.

govern.name: Governance
govern.gloss: The controls that make automated decisions safe, explainable and legible.

stories.head: Tealium + Jev: Real-time AI decisioning without the LLM cost
stories.plain: Tealium's CDP calls Jev, a lightweight AI decision model, to pick the next best action after a cart abandonment — skipping a full large-language model and cutting inference costs. This matters because it shows a practical, cheaper path to real-time agentic decisioning inside an existing customer data stack, which changes the build-vs-buy calculus for marketing teams.

stories.head: Pega CFO: biggest AI budget waste is automating routine rules-based work
stories.plain: Pega's CFO Ken Stillwell argues that most enterprise AI spend goes on automating work that simple rules could handle at a fraction of the cost. He outlines proxy ROI measures and a discipline for shutting down projects that don't deliver. Practical financial framing like this directly shapes how AI projects are approved and governed inside large marketing orgs.

stories.head: Verndale launches AI Visibility services to help brands show up inside AI-generated answers
stories.plain: Verndale is offering a new service that audits whether a brand is named, recommended, and accurately described inside AI assistant answers, then fixes the gaps. As AI-generated answers increasingly replace search results, being present in those answers is becoming a core marketing priority. This is a direct, commercially available response to the GEO challenge.

stories.head: Bazaarvoice: ads buy placement but can't buy belief in AI-answer era
stories.plain: Doug Straton from Bazaarvoice argues that user-generated content and authentic reviews — not paid ads — determine whether an AI assistant recommends a brand. As AI answers displace traditional search rankings, how marketers earn credibility signals rather than just buy placement is a fundamental strategic shift affecting budgets and content strategy.

stories.head: Algolia acquires Velou to add AI product intelligence across search, recommendations and agents
stories.plain: Algolia bought Velou, whose AI enriches product catalogs with retail taxonomy and a product graph, feeding better data to search, recommendations, and AI shopping agents for 18,000 customers. This is a structural change to how product data powers both personalization and agentic shopping, making it relevant to anyone building AI-driven commerce or recommendation systems.

stories.head: Tealium + Jev demo: real-time AI decisioning after cart abandonment — no LLM bill
stories.plain: Tealium shows how its CDP can call Jev, a lightweight AI decision model, to pick a next-best action in real time after a cart abandonment — without routing every decision through an expensive large language model. This matters because it demonstrates a cost-efficient path to agentic decisioning at scale, which changes how marketers budget for real-time personalization.

stories.head: Pega CFO Ken Stillwell: biggest AI budget waste is automating routine, rules-based work
stories.plain: Pega's CFO and COO breaks down where enterprise AI spend goes wrong — chiefly, using costly AI to do work that simple rules already handle. He offers proxy ROI measures and criteria for shutting down failing AI projects. Directly useful for anyone evaluating or approving a marketing AI budget, and rare candor from a C-suite operator inside a major platform vendor.

stories.head: Algolia acquires Velou to embed AI product intelligence across search, recommendations and agents
stories.plain: Algolia is folding Velou's AI-powered catalog enrichment and product graph into its platform used by 18,000 customers, covering search, recommendations, personalization, and its Agent Studio. This is a real product acquisition that extends how AI agents understand and surface products — directly affecting how brands are bought and built on top of Algolia.

stories.head: Verndale launches AI visibility and content supply chain services to help brands appear in AI-generated answers
stories.plain: Verndale is offering a new service layer to audit and improve whether brands are named, recommended, and accurately described inside AI-generated search answers. As AI assistants increasingly replace traditional search for research and buying decisions, this is a concrete commercial service built around Generative Engine Optimization — a fast-growing governance and content challenge for marketing teams.

stories.head: FouAnalytics and fraud0 deploy AI agent that automatically recovers wasted Google Ads spend
stories.plain: The partnership goes beyond measurement: an AI agent now automatically files for and recovers Google Ads refunds caused by invalid traffic, on behalf of large brand advertisers globally. This shifts ad-fraud remediation from a manual reporting task to an autonomous action loop — a meaningful example of agentic AI changing how media budgets are governed and recovered.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: The Enterprise AI Readiness Gap Is the Real Blocker
body: Executives across MarTech are discovering that the technology is no longer the limiting factor — internal readiness is. Typeface's Jamie Garverick and Pega's Ken Stillwell both flag that most enterprise AI budgets are quietly dominated by automating routine, rules-based work rather than genuine transformation.

The implication for decision-makers is stark: before buying another AI platform, audit whether your data, workflows, and teams are actually prepared to use it. Buying AI without readiness is spending on a capability you cannot yet capture.
ev: Agile Brand · Typeface CRO on readiness gap
Agile Brand · Pega CFO on AI budgets

themes.head: Agentic AI Moves from Concept to Product
body: Cisco's new agentic collaboration experiences and Algolia's acquisition of Velou both signal that autonomous, multi-step AI agents are shipping as real products, not just roadmap promises. These agents operate across search, recommendation, and workflow layers — collapsing tasks that previously required human handoffs.

For marketers, this means vendor selection is shifting: the question is no longer 'does it use AI?' but 'can its agents act on my behalf across my full stack without constant supervision?' Platforms that cannot answer yes will lose deals to those that can.
ev: Agile Brand · Algolia acquires Velou for AI agents

themes.head: AI Content Supply Chain Becomes a Managed Service
body: Verndale's new AI Visibility & Content Supply Chain services and Stensul's personalization-at-scale push show that content operations are being industrialised through AI. The goal is to move content from a creative bottleneck to a continuously optimised pipeline that feeds every channel automatically.

This reframes the role of the content team: instead of producing individual assets, they govern templates, rules, and signals. Marketers who restructure around supply-chain thinking will outpace those still commissioning content piece by piece.
ev: MarTech Series · Verndale content supply chain
Agile Brand · Stensul personalization at scale

themes.head: Ad Fraud & Transparency Force Accountability Into Automation
body: FouAnalytics and fraud0 partnering to deliver automated Google Ads refunds — and Vresk labelling every AI-generated answer with its source — reflect a single pressure: buyers are demanding verifiable proof, not just vendor assurances. Transparency is becoming a product feature, not a compliance footnote.

For CMOs this means procurement of AI & ad-tech must now include auditability requirements. Vendors who cannot show their working — whether on ad spend or AI outputs — will face both financial clawbacks and loss of trust.
ev: MarTech Series · Vresk source-labelled AI workspace

themes.head: Rebrands Must Behave Differently, Not Just Look Different
body: Optimizely's Greg Heinz and Bazaarvoice's Doug Straton make complementary arguments: a new visual identity means nothing if the underlying experience & proof points do not change, and advertising can buy placement but cannot manufacture belief. In an AI-saturated media environment, authenticity signals are amplified or destroyed faster than ever.

The strategic shift here is that brand investment must now be measured by behaviour change — in the company and in customers — not by creative awards. Teams using AI to personalise at scale while ignoring earned trust are building on sand.
ev: Agile Brand · Bazaarvoice ads vs belief

month.takeaway: Across every category this month, the common signal is that AI capability is now abundant but the trust, readiness, and accountability infrastructure to use it well is not — and that gap is where the next wave of MarTech competition will be decided.
